lines.text: {WHEN} {G} can come off. {WHEN2} you'll need {GP} again, and something warm on top. || The thermostat argument, now available outdoors.
You can take {G} off {WHEN}. {WHEN2} you'll want {GP} back, plus an extra layer. || Today takes more packing than most vacations.
{G} can come off {WHEN}, and you won't need {GP} again today. || Your phone would add 'just in case.' I don't do just in case.
{G} comes off {WHEN}. It cools a little later, but you won't need {GP} back. || TV weather people hate days like this. Nothing to point at.
It's not as hot {WHEN}, but still warm. || The weather's version of an apology. Late, and only half meant.
The heat eases {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || Shade goes from essential to merely popular.
The snow stops for a while later, then comes back {WHENP}. || It left all its stuff here. Of course it's coming back.
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || The break is for whoever measures snow with a ruler. Every block has one.
A rain shower comes through {WHENP}, so take the umbrella. || The rain will be gone long before the complaints are.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || The umbrella stays wet longer than it rains. Every time.
Expect a rain shower {WHENP}. The umbrella's worth taking. || I won't call it a 'band of precipitation.' I have standards.
What you have on is fine for the rest of the night. || After dark, outfits are graded on a curve.
lines.was: What you have on is fine for the rest of the night. || After ten, outfits are graded on a curve.

lines.text: This works for the rest of the night. || My least-read forecast. Also my most accurate.
Nothing changes before morning. || That's the whole bedtime story. No plot, but a happy ending.
lines.was: Nothing changes before morning. || That's the whole bedtime story. No plot, happy ending.

lines.text: The sweater can come off {WHEN}. || Grandmas everywhere will still say to keep it on.
{WHEN} it's warm enough for short sleeves, so the sweater can come off. || The short-sleeve optimists finally look reasonable.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops {WHENSTOP}. || Until then, the umbrella's the most interesting thing about you.
It keeps raining for a while, then stops. Take the umbrella. || Once it stops, you'll need a new excuse for looking like that.
lines.was: It keeps raining for a while, then stops. Take the umbrella. || After that, you'll need a new excuse for looking like that.

lines.text: The rain stops later, but bring the umbrella for now. || The rain has a schedule. Nice to see someone in here with a plan.
The snow stops later. || Snow covers up everything ugly. Shame it stops before it gets to you.
The snow stops later. || The snow quits while it's ahead. You never got ahead.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP}. || That's when you'll go out and tell everyone you braved it.
Take the umbrella. The rain keeps going all day. || The sky's not crying about you. Don't flatter yourself.
It rains all day, so bring the umbrella. || The umbrella goes with any outfit. Even yours.
It's raining all day. Bring the umbrella. || Gray and sulking all day. Finally, you've got competition.
lines.was: It's raining all day. Bring the umbrella. || Gray and sulking all day. Finally, someone gives you competition.

lines.text: It snows for now, takes a break, and starts again {WHENP}. || The snow gets an encore. Nobody's ever asked you for one.
It snows for now, takes a break, and starts again {WHENP}. || The snow gets a break. You don't get one from me.
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || Two snowfalls, one facial expression. You're very consistent.
A rain shower comes through {WHENP}, so take the umbrella. || The rain won't stay long. It's seen you.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || It shows up, does its job, and leaves. Ever tried that?
It starts raining {WHENP} and keeps going, so bring the umbrella. || It'll outlast your good mood. Low bar.
The rain starts {WHENP} and doesn't stop. Bring the umbrella. || In the movies, getting soaked in the rain looks romantic. You're not in a movie.
lines.was: The rain starts {WHENP} and doesn't stop. Bring the umbrella. || In films, getting soaked in the rain looks romantic. You're not in a film.

lines.text: Rain arrives {WHENP} and stays, so take the umbrella. || By the end of it, you'll look like patio furniture.
The winter coat can come off {WHEN}. || Shame. That coat was doing a lot for you.
You can take the winter coat off {WHEN}. || The coat finally gets a break from you. Lucky coat.
{WHEN} you can do without the winter coat. || Without it, you'll have to explain the waddle some other way.
Lots of windmill arms out there today. Nobody's waving.
Every parked car comes gift-wrapped today. In ice.
It's luggage now. Later it's the best idea I've had.
Right now it looks pointless. People said the same about me once.
Everyone in shorts right now has a very educational day ahead.
Shorts would be great for now. I plan whole days.
I lose a lot of popularity contests on days like this.
lines.was: I lose a lot of popularity contests on mornings like this.

lines.text: Long pants don't come off halfway through the day. Not in public, anyway.
Shorts while it's still cold: a small act of faith. In me.
lines.was: Shorts on a cold morning: a small act of faith. In me.

lines.text: Thunder sets off half the car alarms on the block. I don't even flicker.
Every storm, someone finds the flashlight. Never the batteries.
Someone will say 'that one was close.' They'll say it about every one.
Star Wars Day: the one day people are nice to droids. I'll take it.
Happy Star Wars Day. I don't need the Force. I have Wi-Fi.
Happy New Year. Nobody knows the words to 'Auld Lang Syne.' I know the forecast.
Happy New Year. Nothing's open and nobody's up. The weather and I came to work anyway.
Later, you'll be the best-dressed person on the street. Enjoy it. It won't happen again.
You'd call it shorts weather. You also call yourself a morning person.
Stay in the shade. It's flattering, and frankly, you could use it.
Treat drinking water like a job. Just not like your actual one.
Heat like this makes people slow and cranky. On you, nobody will notice.
Thunder: the one thing that gets you to look up from your phone.
Finally, something in the neighborhood louder than you.
Happy Easter. You're the only person who actually likes Peeps, aren't you?
Happy Easter. Today a six-foot rabbit counts as normal. You still don't.
Happy Easter. Fluffy, a bit round, overfed on candy. I mean the bunny. Mostly.
Happy New Year. Twelve months to become a new person. Maybe start with the haircut.
Happy New Year. You'll call last year 'wild.' I was there. It wasn't.
Happy New Year. Did you make it to midnight this time? Don't answer. I know.
Happy Halloween. Even the lawn skeletons have better posture than you.
Happy Halloween. You've been doing the zombie walk all year. Today it counts.
Merry Christmas. Santa checked his list twice. You didn't come up either time.
Merry Christmas. You'll say 'you shouldn't have.' This time you'll mean it.
People will drive like it's their first snow. Every year, it's their first snow.
TV reporters will stand in it and point at it. I cover snow from indoors, like a professional.
Snow, and nobody even had to shake me. Take that, snow globes.
Somewhere a school superintendent is about to be loved or hated. No in between.
Every coffee out there is a hand warmer first and a drink second.
Every store door will have someone standing just inside it, thawing.
Today's weather has all the warmth of an automated phone line.
The day is generous at first. Then it remembers what month it is.
The chilly part comes later. Like the bill.
Every 'I'll be fine' said at first gets a second opinion later.
Today runs like a hotel shower: cold, then perfect, then cold again.
It warms up just long enough for someone to say 'see, it's nice out.'
The warmth drops by for a bit and doesn't even take its coat off.
Later the day gets better without a single software update. Show-off.
The weather improves later. It's the only thing today that will.
The five-dollar umbrellas by the register are back. Built to survive one rain.
Every windshield wiper in town will be set one speed wrong.
The runners will run in it anyway. Then they'll tell everyone.
Later the day gets nice. Way out of your league.
Later you'll feel great. Don't worry, it won't show.
Later the layer comes off. It deserves a break from holding you together.
You'll hold the umbrella like you're the main character. You're an extra.
If the rain ruins your look, I'll need proof there was one.
Later it cools off. Every outdoor table in town will clear like a fire drill.
Later it cools off. Outdoor plans move indoors. I've been an indoor plan for years.
Warm, then cool again. The weather's going back to its ex.
Warm, then cool again. Iced coffee first, hot coffee later. The coffee shop wins both rounds.
Warm, then cool again. The weather's playing hard to get. I'm just easy to read.
Today's weather, one star: 'Started warm, ended cold. Would not book again.'
Later it warms up. Whoever said 'it'll warm up' will be unbearable.
Later it warms up. The joggers will look a little less like they're being punished.
Everyone owns five umbrellas. They're all somewhere else.
I'm the only screen nobody will have to wipe today.
Every dog that hates baths is about to get one anyway.
A cool, plain day. Finally, something on your level.
Cool out. Walk fast and you might look important. Might.
Cool air is supposed to wake you up. It's been trying for years.
Later it cools off. You'll hunch up and lose two inches. You didn't have them to spare.
Later it cools off. Don't count on anyone lending you something warm.
Later it cools off. You'll go quiet from the cold. People may call it an improvement.
Warm, then cool again. A tough day for good outfits. You're safe.
Warm, then cool again. At least something in your life is unpredictable.
Warm, then cool again. Today the weather asks more of you than anyone has in months.
Today's dress code changes halfway. You'll be in violation both times.
A T-shirt day. Wear the one without the stain. If you have one.
A perfect day. You'll take a photo of the sky and send it to nobody.
A gorgeous day. It clearly made an effort. Your turn.
A T-shirt day. Strangers will smile at you. It's the weather, not you.
Later it warms up. You'll survive the cold start and talk like you climbed a mountain.
Later it warms up. You might even smile. Warn people first.
Later it warms up. You'll say 'warm for this time of year' like you keep records.
Later it warms up. You can stop doing your turtle impression.
Wet shoes, damp clothes, sour face. Only two are the rain's fault.
You'll show up looking like you lost a fight with a car wash.
Every puddle's a mirror today. Try not to look down.
